CBS News Chief Bari Weiss Defends 60 Minutes Ratings, Calls Show 'Tremendously Well' Despite Decline

29 Oct 2026, 06:37 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

चित्र: www.theguardian.com — Creative Commons

Ratings Decline Sparks Concern

CBS News editor‑in‑chief Bari Weiss has publicly addressed for the first time the viewership challenges the network has faced during her year‑long tenure. The flagship Sunday program, 60 Minutes, has struggled to match last season’s average of 9.1 million viewers per episode. Variety reported that the most recent episode drew just 5.64 million viewers, described as “one of the smallest audiences for the program in years” and the lowest‑rated sixth episode of the weekly show this century.

Weiss's Response at Industry Conference

Weiss spoke at an industry conference organized by the tech publication The Information on Wednesday. When asked about diminished viewership, she sidestepped the concern, stating that focusing on precise audience numbers “would never allow me to build anything.” She emphasized that the show was performing “tremendously well” overall and that 60 Minutes was not her top priority.

> “I could never build anything if I were focused on the precise number of people that happen to tune in to the second feature on 60 Minutes on a given Sunday,” Weiss said.

Recent Viewership Numbers

The show’s performance is highly variable. While the 4 October edition attracted more than 10 million total viewers, other episodes have fallen well below the 9 million benchmark. The program’s ratings are also heavily dependent on the preceding NFL football game; a strong pre‑show rating can lift overall numbers, but recent weeks have shown inconsistent results despite high‑profile guest bookings and news‑making segments.

Leadership Changes and Network Strategy

Weiss overhauled 60 Minutes in late May, removing the show’s executive producer and parting ways with three top correspondents, including veteran Scott Pelley. The restructuring was intended to revitalize the brand, but the immediate impact on viewership remains mixed. Weiss described her approach as “putting the blinders on, tuning out the noise and focusing,” noting that she is not pursuing her work for popularity.

Parent Company Merger Context

The article also touches on the broader corporate landscape. CBS News’ parent company, Skydance, recently merged with Warner Bros Discovery, the parent of CNN. Although there were rumors that Weiss might lead CNN, CEO David Ellison kept incumbent CNN chief Mark Thompson in place. Weiss reiterated her focus on CBS News, calling it “a big enough challenge.”

Practical Implications for CBS and Viewers

  • Advertising Revenue: Lower viewership can affect ad rates, a key revenue driver for CBS News. However, the show’s occasional spikes (e.g., the 10 million‑viewer October episode) suggest that strong content can still attract large audiences.
  • Programming Decisions: The dependence on NFL lead‑ins highlights the network’s reliance on external programming. Future scheduling may need to balance high‑profile games with content that can sustain viewership independently.
  • Talent Retention: The departure of senior correspondents could impact the show’s credibility and depth of reporting, potentially influencing long‑term audience trust.

What’s Confirmed and What Remains Unknown

Confirmed:

  • Weiss publicly addressed ratings concerns for the first time.
  • Recent episode viewership figures (5.64 million) were reported by Variety.
  • Leadership changes in May included the removal of the executive producer and three correspondents.
  • Skydance’s merger with Warner Bros Discovery has occurred, and CNN leadership remains unchanged.

Unknown:

  • The exact criteria Weiss is using to evaluate the show’s success beyond overall “tremendously well.”
  • Whether the restructuring will produce measurable improvements in upcoming seasons.
  • The long‑term impact of the merger on CBS News’ editorial independence or resource allocation.

How Readers Can Verify

The statements quoted above come from Weiss’s remarks at the Information conference and are reported in The Guardian’s coverage. Readers can review the original article at: [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/28/bari-weiss-cbs-news-60-minutes](https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/28/bari-weiss-cbs-news-60-minutes) Additional viewership data referenced by Variety can be cross‑checked through industry rating reports such as Nielsen or the Broadcast Data System.
